annotations.title: Check a keyword's Naver AI briefing and search results

description: Naver search only. Looks each keyword up on Naver's integrated search through the person's uplika Chrome extension (it reads the public result page in their own browser, about 3 seconds apart; no window opens) and returns, per keyword, whether an AI briefing answers it and in which form, the briefing's body sources (rank, site, title, how many answer paragraphs cite each) and image sources, where the blog posts sit in the integrated search results, and the related questions. Pass blog to mark that blog's posts (mine: true) and get its verdict per keyword (bodyRank, imageRank, citedParagraphs, organicRank, organicArea). Up to 10 keywords. A keyword read in the last 30 minutes comes from the saved result unless fresh is true; new reads spend the person's daily allowance of 200 Naver search pages. It waits up to 60 seconds. When it answers partial: true with pending[], the extension keeps reading the rest in the background; calling again with the same keywords later returns the saved results instead of reading them twice. The answer also carries citationRules: sentence rules Uplika measured on posts the AI briefing quoted, to check a draft against as their own layer (they are not Naver's criteria). Which posts Naver cites is Naver's choice; this only reports what the page shows at that moment.

blog.description: A Naver blog id or any link to the blog, to mark its posts and judge them.

fresh.description: Read again even if this keyword was read in the last 30 minutes (spends the daily allowance).

keywords.description: 1-10 keywords, as a reader would search them.

workspaceId.description: Which workspace this is for. Only needed when the account has more than one — the error tells you the ids when it matters. Leave it out if it is already decided; do not ask the person again.
